description: We are Las Vacas Cósmicas, a fun, multidisciplinary team from Colombia: an economist, an electronics engineer, a microbiologist, a computer engineering student and an and our youngest member, an eighth-grade student. We love learning, laughing and building useful things. For COW-FARM we set strict rules: never invent data, show every source and label our estimates. We joined Space Apps to give our very best and help farmers make better decisions with NASA data.
summary:
COW-FARM is a FREE mobile web application that enables farmers to compare three different rotation options for their field. You draw your field on the map and confirm the soil type and set your 8 priorities (water, income, erosion etc). It uses NASA Earth Observations (Climate (NASA POWER), Vegetation (MODIS), Elevation (SRTM)). You will be presented with reasons and evidence for why the rotation option has been recommended, what benefits you can expect, gaps in data and any risks which should be discussed locally. With the market section you have market signals to consider before planting.

This is important for farmers who are having to adapt to changing rainfall and heat patterns. COW-FARM is simply a tool to help you make decisions. All data shown has a source and time frame. Any estimated data is clearly marked and data gaps will show as no data. The application can be used in Spanish, English and French.
details:
The COW-FARM app drives the user through 8 sections; Field, Soil, Priorities, Conditions, Climate Outlook, Strategies, Simulator and Market to produce a comparison of 3 strategies for the selected field. This will always include the strategy currently being used. If the crops are perennial (coffee, avocado, oil palm etc.) then an additiona cover crop is recommended.

The COW-FARM app works as follows:

Field: Draw a polygon, upload a contour file, search for a place or use your devices location. Can be used anywhere on the globe.

Soil: The soil type will be automatically read from ISRIC SoilGrids. This includes clay, sand, silt, organic carbon and pH. Manual correction can be made. The soil type will also check that the total percentages = 100% and will show what the soil is classified as by the USDA.

Priorities: Water, Income, Soil Health, Erosion, Drought, Inputs, Carbon Organic Matter and Pests and Diseases.

Conditions: Temperature, Rainfall, Solar Radiation and Soils Moisture will be read from NASA POWER. Vegetation (NDVI) from MODIS and if this is not available, Copernicus Sentinel-2. Elevation and Slope will be read from SRTM. An estimate for reference evapotranspiration will be calculated using the Hargreaves-Samani Method.

Outlook: A 3 month climate outlook will be generated from the data provided by NASA POWER from 1991. A probability of what could happen (Tercile, trend and persistence).

Strategies: Crop Profiles will be scored to match the field and priorities. There are 51 crop profiles that will be matched to the field. This will show you why it was recommended, evidence, the benefits, what information is missing and risk factors that need to be reviewed locally.

Simulator: Change assumptions for rainfall, temperature and irrigation and see how this affects the comparison.

Market: Production, Area Harvested, Yield, Trade and Prices for 44 crops. There are approximately 560,000 observations that have been uploaded from FAOSTAT, World Bank Pink Sheet and Colombia's municipal agriculture survey (EVA).

The benefits of our app are the following:

* NASA data translated into something that can be used. This is simple to understand and can be used on a phone.

* Transparent about uncertainty. Any values we have had to estimate will be marked as estimates by the team. This reduces confidence. Data from NASA POWER is an indication of what will happen in the area (the area covers approximately 50km grid) not the exact field.

* All data is transparent. It will show what the data is from, link, when it was published, time frame, what area it is for and unit of measure. No conversions of currencies will be made and price types will not be compared.

* Never states that a crop is profitable. Crops will need to pass both agricultural and commercial reviews.

* Live source status panel. Shows what services are returning data.

We hope that the producers workers will be able to try out changing their rotation strategy without having to commit to a whole season. They will also be able to clearly see what they cannot know from the data, and it is advisable to seek agronomic advice.

We rely on various tools and technologies for this creation:

App: Built using React, Typescript, TailwindCSS and TanStack Start Server Functions. Using Lovable. Maps using Leaflet and Leaflet-Geoman. Charts using Recharts. Translations using react-i18next.

Recommendation Engine: Pure Typescript functions with unit testing using Vitest.

Data: Supabase (PostgreSQL) as Database engine filled with NASA data.

Data Pipeline: Python and Pandas run in Google Colab. Dry run mode, crop matching review and automated quality checks.

AI: Lovable, Claude and ChatGPT. Used for coding, text and team images.
